summary: Pinned-version shadowing after shard pre-initialization triggers silent fallback and tokenization mismatch
description:
Issue summary: VelosHealth observed sudden production degradations for a subset of pinned sessions after a background shard pre-initialization (prewarm) job ran during a low-traffic window. The tenant reported mixed-model responses (some calls returned the pinned variant, others silently routed to a degraded fallback variant) and an elevated tokenization mismatch error rate for streaming requests.

Impact: ~8% of requests from the affected tenant returned responses from the fallback variant resulting in content regressions. Some streaming sessions ended with tokenization mismatch errors causing aborted streams. Customer-facing SLA impacted for pinned sessions.

Environment: Production (dedicated cluster), us-west-2, dedicated pool velos-prod-pool-3. Pinned model: redwood-7b-v2 pinned at 2026-03-14T01:04Z. Canary prewarm job ran at 2026-03-14T01:05Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed by SRE):
1) Start a pinned session with pin header X-Model-Pin: redwood-7b-v2 for a Velos tenant.
2) Trigger a streaming request with medium prompt lengths (~120 tokens).
3) While session active, run background shard pre-initialization (prewarm) of redwood-7b-q4_0 on the same dedicated pool.
4) Observe intermittent routing to fallback variant and occasional tokenization mismatch errors in stream.

Observed behavior: Interleaved responses where ~92% aligned with pinned version and ~8% executed on a fallback variant (redwood-7b-q4_0). Edge logs show pin binding for the session still present, but orchestrator routing snapshots include a short-lived alias mapping that reassigns some requests to the fallback. KV cache entries show a tokenization length delta for the fallback variant leading to mismatched stream framing.

Expected behavior: Pinned sessions should maintain strict affinity to the pinned model variant for the session lifetime. Background prewarm should not introduce transient routing aliases or tokenization deltas that trigger fallback.

Initial hypothesis: The shard pre-initialization preloaded metadata and temporarily exposed a shadow alias in the routing snapshot before the orchestrator finished committing the pin-coherence update. Edge/ingress used the intermediate snapshot for a small set of requests, causing a silent fallback. Additionally, model quantization differences (v2 vs q4_0) caused tokenization framing differences that surfaced as stream mismatch errors.

References: edge logs (link in investigation_notes), orchestration snapshots (ORB IDs referenced in investigation_notes), metrics dashboard: /dashboards/tenant/velos/pinning-heatmap.
comments: 2026-03-14 02:10 UTC - VelosHealth (customer): We're seeing some sessions return different model outputs randomly. These are pinned sessions; we expect strict pinning. Several streaming calls also failed mid-stream with framing errors. Please advise.

2026-03-14 02:18 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Thanks for reporting. We're triaging. Can you share a sample request-id and approximate timestamps? We're checking routing snapshots and ingestion logs now.
2026-03-14 02:30 UTC - Customer: Sample request-id: req-velos-98a3fd (approx 2026-03-14T01:06:12Z). More occurrences around 01:05-01:10Z.

2026-03-14 03:05 UTC - SRE (Oliver Grant): Found orchestrator snapshot churn during prewarm window. Some snapshots included a temporary alias mapping (alias: pool-shadow-rc-13) that points to q4 variant. Edge cache TTL is 30s; a race allowed an intermediate snapshot to be used for a subset of connections.

2026-03-14 03:34 UTC - Serving Eng (Priya Kapoor): Confirmed tokenization length delta between redwood-7b-v2 and redwood-7b-q4_0 when using the same tokenizer metadata. Quantized variant returns different token boundaries for certain multi-byte tokens leading to stream framing errors.
investigation_notes: Edge request traces (req-velos-98a3fd): ingress -> edge-proxy 01:06:11.834Z, snapshot_id: snap-20260314-010604-v2 (committed), then a subsequent request used snapshot_id: snap-20260314-010607-shadow (intermediate) which included alias pool-shadow-rc-13.

Orchestrator logs show prewarm job start at 01:05:47Z; metadata push completed at 01:06:08Z, but commit_ack to control-plane delayed until 01:06:10Z due to transient etcd latency. Control-plane published intermediate routing snapshot at 01:06:07Z containing temporary alias for the shard while prewarm finished.

KV cache entries: keys for session tokenization show two differing 'frame_length' values (v2=16, q4_0=14) for identical prompts, explaining streaming mismatch errors when a fallback variant served the mid-stream request.

Traffic distribution analysis: 95% requests served on stable snapshot, 5-10% routed via intermediate snapshot. Affected sessions were those with long-lived streaming connections that spanned the snapshot churn window.
No evidence of explicit unpin API calls. No quota/rate limit spikes. Autoscaler not involved; capacity steady for pool.

Related config change: canary prewarm orchestration PR merged yesterday (serving-runtime #4298) which modified prewarm workflow to publish a 'shadow' alias to enable warm standby. That alias should have been guarded by feature flag but was active in velos-prod-pool-3 during the run.
Repro attempt in staging: reproduced by running prewarm job with timing adjusted to create snapshot commit race; confirmed edge cache TTL and intermediate snapshot selection as root cause.
Logs and traces: s3://redwood-logs/prod/velos/2026-03-14/req-velos-98a3fd.log, trace link: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abc123 (access restricted to eng).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-14 04:10 UTC): Scoped rollback of the prewarm shadow-alias feature flag in us-west-2 and immediate edge cache purge for velos-prod-pool-3. Force rebind issued to pinned sessions (control-plane command: REBIND_PIN tenant=velos model=redwood-7b-v2). This restored >99.9% pin coherence within 90s.

Short-term mitigation: Increase snapshot publication atomicity by holding intermediate aliases until commit_ack received. Edge teams purged TTL caches and implemented a short-term TTL reduce to 5s for the next 2 hours to minimize intermediate snapshot exposure.

Permanent fix plan: Revert the shadow-alias auto-publish behavior in PR #4298, add orchestrator guard to ensure prewarm metadata cannot be included in routing snapshots until commit handshake completes, and add a regression test that simulates prewarm timing races with streaming sessions.

Owner for fix: Serving Eng (Priya Kapoor) + Orchestrator (Diego Morales). Target patch release: 2026-03-18. Canary rollout plan: canary in staging -> controlled production rollout on weekend window with monitoring of pin-coherence metric and streaming error-rate.
Customer communication: Sent interim update to VelosHealth (03:25 UTC) describing workaround and plan. Follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC postmortem call and delivery of RCA and action items.

Follow-ups/Action items: (1) Add unit/integration tests for pin-coherence on prewarm path; (2) Add dashboard alert for snapshot-churn-to-pin-fallback ratio; (3) Review edge cache TTL semantics for snapshot transitions.
